events.title: Battle of Chickamauga Concludes
events.description: After two days of ferocious fighting in northwest Georgia, Confederate forces under Braxton Bragg drove Union troops under William Rosecrans from the field on September 20. George H. Thomas's stand on Snodgrass Hill, which earned him the nickname the Rock of Chickamauga, saved the Union army from total collapse.
events.significance: It was the Confederacy's greatest victory in the Western Theater and one of the bloodiest battles of the Civil War, with the second-highest casualty toll after Gettysburg.

events.title: Chester A. Arthur Becomes President
events.description: One day after James Garfield died from an assassin's bullet, Chester A. Arthur took the presidential oath of office in New York City, becoming the 21st President of the United States.
events.significance: Arthur, once seen as a machine politician, went on to champion civil service reform by signing the Pendleton Act of 1883, a turning point in American government.

events.title: The First Cannes Film Festival Opens
events.description: The inaugural Cannes International Film Festival opened on the French Riviera, bringing filmmakers and stars together after the Second World War.
events.significance: Cannes grew into the world's most prestigious film festival, shaping global cinema and launching countless careers.

events.title: Billie Jean King Wins the 'Battle of the Sexes'
events.description: At the Houston Astrodome, tennis champion Billie Jean King defeated former men's champion Bobby Riggs in straight sets before a huge live crowd and a vast television audience.
events.significance: The victory became a landmark moment for women's equality in sports and boosted the fight for equal pay and opportunity in athletics.
